description: Device results for haptic feedback on the mobile web, one record per device/browser combination tested. null means not recorded or not verified; it is never a guess. See README.md for the test rows.

records.notes: Exact model and iOS version not recorded; the phone was on a current iOS release in 2026-11. navigator.vibrate is undefined. Only a real finger on a real switch ticked; every script-initiated toggle was silent. The drag result is from a horizontal number dial with touch-action: none on the switch: one tick per step while dragging and one tick on a tap. touch-action: pan-y runs in code and in emulation but was not confirmed on a device. In-app browsers on iOS were not tested for the drag technique. Public reports (the READMEs of jcruzfff/haptick and tijnjh/ios-haptics) say script-toggled switch haptics were blocked in iOS 26.5; not checked across iOS versions here.
navigator.vibrate(ms) worked inside WeChat's in-app browser.

Pulse-length round; the browser used was not recorded. The first rounds produced no vibration at all because vibration was switched off on the phone (silent-mode icon in the status bar), while navigator.vibrate still returned true. Every conclusion from before that was found is void: an early belief that 6 ms is too short to play was formed with vibration off and was never re-tested, so 6 ms is untested; pulses shorter than 18 ms were not re-tested with vibration on. With vibration on, 18 ms was judged the best per-step tick.

Vibration plays but does not feel like a crisp click at the lengths tried (the lengths are not listed in these notes). The tester assumes the phone lacks a linear motor; not checked against a spec sheet. A web page can set only the pulse length (no amplitude, no waveform), so there was nothing to tune beyond duration; left at 18 ms. Browser and OS version not recorded.
